chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Halal said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not fast for three days after the Feast of Sacrifice (Al-Adha) and do not fast for three days after the Feast of Breaking the Fast (Al-Fitr), for they are days of eating and drinking.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ أَكْلٍ وَشُرْبٍ: Days of eating and drinking (celebratory days)
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: The Feast of Breaking the Fast (Eid al-Fitr)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting in the three days following Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) prohibits voluntary fasting for three days immediately following Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr, designating these periods as days of celebration and feasting. This ruling, found in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that these specific days are meant for joyous consumption rather than asceticism, aligning with the prophetic tradition of 'days of eating and drinking.'
